NAME: Customer Data Quality Gate
DESC:
Before loading a customer extract into the warehouse, the team wants a quality gate: valid rows are cleaned and loaded, invalid rows are kept aside with the reason of their rejection, so that the source team can fix them.

Input

customers_raw_df (all columns are raw text)

column type description
customer_id string may be null, blank, or padded with spaces
email string may be null
age string may be null; at most 6 characters
country string may be null

Rules

Check the rules below in this order. The first rule that fails gives the reject_reason of the row; a row that passes all rules is valid. Every input row ends up in exactly one of the two outputs.

order reject_reason the row is rejected when
1 missing_id customer_id is null or empty after trimming
2 duplicate_id the trimmed customer_id appears in more than one row of the input (all those rows are rejected)
3 invalid_email email is null, or the trimmed email does not match the regex ^[^@\s]+@[^@\s]+\.[^@\s]+$
4 invalid_age age is not null and, after trimming, is not made only of digits 0-9, or its value is greater than 120
5 invalid_country country is null, or the trimmed country is not exactly 2 letters A-Z / a-z

A null age is valid (the age is unknown).

Output

solve returns a tuple (valid_df, rejected_df).

valid_df: cleaned values, exactly these columns, in this order:

column type value
customer_id string trimmed
email string trimmed and lowercased
age int integer value of the trimmed age, or null
country string trimmed and uppercased

rejected_df: original values (unchanged) plus the reason, exactly these columns, in this order:

column type
customer_id string
email string
age string
country string
reject_reason string

The row order of both DataFrames does not matter.

customers_raw_df

customer_id email age country

"C2" "omar@mail" "28" "FR"
"C3" "sara@mail.fr" "abc" "FR"

"C6" "c6@a.io" "200" "MA"

Expected valid_df

customer_id email age country
C1 amina@mail.com 34 MA
C4 c4@mail.ma null ES

Expected rejected_df

customer_id email age country reject_reason
"C2" "omar@mail" "28" "FR" invalid_email
"C3" "sara@mail.fr" "abc" "FR" invalid_age
null "x@y.z" "20" "MA" missing_id
"C5" "c5@mail.ma" "40" "France" invalid_country
"C6" "c6@a.io" "200" "MA" invalid_age
"C7" "a@b.co" "22" "MA" duplicate_id
"C7 " "other@b.co" "23" "US" duplicate_id

Function signature

from pyspark.sql import DataFrame
from typing import Tuple

def solve(customers_raw_df: DataFrame) -> Tuple[DataFrame, DataFrame]:
    ...

Constraints

  • Use the PySpark DataFrame API. No pandas, no collect(), no Python UDFs.
  • Your code is run with Spark's ANSI mode enabled (spark.sql.ansi.enabled=true, the default since Spark 4.0): in this mode, casting an invalid string such as "abc" to int raises an error instead of returning null. Your job must not fail on any input.
  • customers_raw_df has up to 10^7 rows.

In the test results, both DataFrames are shown in one table: the column output says if a row comes from valid or from rejected.

SOLUTION:
from pyspark.sql import DataFrame, Window
from pyspark.sql import functions as F

EMAIL_RE = r"^[^@\s]+@[^@\s]+\.[^@\s]+$"


def solve(customers_raw_df: DataFrame):
    cid = F.trim(F.col("customer_id"))
    email = F.trim(F.col("email"))
    age_txt = F.trim(F.col("age"))
    country = F.upper(F.trim(F.col("country")))

    # Cast protégé : on ne caste que du texte fait de chiffres (sinon, en mode ANSI, cast lève une erreur).
    age_int = F.when(age_txt.rlike(r"^[0-9]+$"), age_txt.cast("int"))

    # Nombre de lignes partageant le même id nettoyé (doublons après trim).
    n_same_id = F.count(F.lit(1)).over(Window.partitionBy(cid))

    # Règles dans l'ordre : la première qui échoue donne le motif. Un when sans otherwise => null = valide.
    reason = (
        F.when(cid.isNull() | (cid == ""), "missing_id")
         .when(n_same_id > 1, "duplicate_id")
         .when(email.isNull() | ~email.rlike(EMAIL_RE), "invalid_email")
         .when(F.col("age").isNotNull() & (age_int.isNull() | (age_int > 120)), "invalid_age")
         .when(country.isNull() | ~country.rlike(r"^[A-Z]{2}$"), "invalid_country")
    )
    tagged = customers_raw_df.withColumn("reject_reason", reason)

    valid_df = tagged.filter(F.col("reject_reason").isNull()).select(
        cid.alias("customer_id"),
        F.lower(email).alias("email"),
        age_int.alias("age"),
        country.alias("country"),
    )
    rejected_df = tagged.filter(F.col("reject_reason").isNotNull()).select(
        "customer_id", "email", "age", "country", "reject_reason"      # valeurs brutes + motif
    )
    return valid_df, rejected_df
WRAPPER:
from pyspark.sql import functions as _KF
def __kata_entry__(customers_raw_df):
    valid, rejected = solve(customers_raw_df)
    v = valid.select("customer_id", "email", _KF.col("age").cast("string").alias("age"), "country",
                     _KF.lit(None).cast("string").alias("reject_reason"), _KF.lit("valid").alias("output"))
    r = rejected.select("customer_id", "email", _KF.col("age").cast("string").alias("age"), "country",
                        "reject_reason", _KF.lit("rejected").alias("output"))
    return v.unionByName(r)
